saints.name: Our Lady of Lourdes
saints.title: Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: The Church remembers the appearances of the Immaculate Virgin to a poor girl at a grotto in the Pyrenees, and the healing spring that welled up there…
biography: On 11 February 1858 the Blessed Virgin appeared at the grotto of Massabielle, near Lourdes in the French Pyrenees, to Bernadette Soubirous, a poor girl of fourteen. It was the first of eighteen apparitions, stretching to 16 July, in which the lady — robed in white, with a blue sash and yellow roses on her feet — called for prayer and penance for sinners.

On 25 February the lady bade Bernadette drink and wash at a spring that welled up where she dug, and asked that a chapel be built and that the people come in procession. On 25 March, the feast of the Annunciation, she gave her name in the local dialect: 'I am the Immaculate Conception' — a title Pope Pius IX had defined as dogma only four years before, in 1854.

After long inquiry the Bishop of Tarbes, Bertrand-Sévère Laurence, declared the apparitions worthy of belief on 18 January 1862. Lourdes grew into one of the greatest pilgrimage shrines of Christendom, drawing millions; its spring has been linked to healings that a medical bureau still examines. Pius X established this feast in 1907, and John Paul II later bound it to the World Day of the Sick.
saints.knownFor: The apparitions of the Immaculate Virgin at Lourdes in 1858.
